chunks: Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who endows an estate, then it appears to him that he should alter something in that. He said:

If he endowed it for a child or for others, then appointed a caretaker for it, he has no right to revoke it. If they were minors and he stipulated its guardianship for them until they reached maturity, so that he would hold it on their behalf, then he has no right to revoke it. But if they were adults and he did not deliver it to them, and they did not dispute with him until they took possession of it from him, then he may revoke it, because they do not take possession of it from him while they have already reached maturity.

key_terms.الضَّيْعَةَ: the estate or landed property being endowed
key_terms.صِغَارًا: minors who have not yet reached maturity
key_terms.قَيِّمًا: a caretaker or administrator appointed over the endowment
key_terms.وِلَايَتَهَا: guardianship or authority over the endowed property
key_terms.يَحُوزُهَا: to take possession of it in a legally effective way
key_terms.يَرْجِعَ: to revoke or withdraw the endowment
key_terms.يُوقِفُ: to dedicate or endow property as waqf

ai.seo_question: When can a person revoke a waqf after endowing a property?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about waqf and when an endowed property becomes binding and no longer revocable. It explains that effective transfer or valid possession on behalf of the beneficiaries determines whether the donor may retract the endowment, especially in cases involving minors and adults.
